text:
Aisha: perfbot alerted +6% p50 token latency on staging overnight, looks tied to KV-cache miss storms and weird kernel switching
Matt: ugh. do we have an nsys capture for the failing run? what flags did you use?
Aisha: yes, i grabbed one quick. command i ran:
```
nsys profile --output=staging_kv_reg --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=12s --force-overwrite --capture-range=nvtx
```
Matt: nice. did you bracket the hot region with NVTX markers or just full-run?
Aisha: bracketed. we push NVTX around the generation loop, then trimmed to the NVTX range. perfbot attached the diff: kernel time jump correlates with a sequence where batch sizes fluctuate and kv hits drop from ~98% to ~72%.
perfbot: nightly/2026-03-17: test=gen-load-64 p50=32ms -> 34ms (+6.25%), p95 similar; capture=qdrp attached to build 2026.03.17-rc3
Nguyen: ok a few quick hypotheses: 1) kernel selection thrash between fast quantized matmul and fallback f32 kernel when sequence length or batch changes; 2) KV cache eviction/alloc path causing extra cudaMallocs; 3) nsys sampling bias if duration too short.
Sofia: for the sampling bias, try longer capture or bracketed short captures with warmup. i usually do: warmup with 8 iterations (no capture), then 6s bracket with NVTX and --duration=6s to keep file small. also disable sampling if you need 100% timeline fidelity: `--sample=none` (or equivalent) and rely on full tracing.
Matt: can you paste the NVTX snippet we used?
Aisha: sure: 
```cpp
nvtxRangePushA("gen_loop_start");
// model step, dispatch kernels, kv load
nvtxRangePop();
```
Nguyen: to inspect kernel decisions, open the qdrep in the timeline view and look for lots of tiny kernels (transpose/copy kernels) between attention matmul calls. that indicates kernel fusion mismatch. also check CUDA stream concurrency: OSRT markers will show many small async ops that add launch overhead.
Sofia: for a focused repro i suggest: fix batch size to 32, pin seq len to 128, force kv hit-rate artificially low and high by toggling the cache bypass flag. capture both runs and diff timelines. that isolates whether the regression is kernel selection or cache path overhead.
Matt: any CLI flags to reduce noise when comparing two captures?
Nguyen: use `nsys export` to csv and then `nsys stats -i capture.qdrep --report=timeline --format=csv` and diff the kernel names/avg durations. also extract memory ops report to see cudaMalloc/cudaFree spikes.
Aisha: actionable next steps: 1) run two bracketed captures (kv-hit and kv-miss) with `--trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` + `--sample=none` 2) export timeline csvs and run a quick python script to aggregate per-kernel p50/p95 3) if we see many small kernels between matmuls -> try enabling aggressive fusion in the runtime or adjust batching heuristics to avoid mid-batch size transitions.
Matt: i'll schedule a short troubleshooting slot after standup and run the double-capture. thanks for the checklist. :thumbsup:
Sofia: FYI if you hit large qdrep sizes, `nsys profile --output=foo --duration=6s --sample=none --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt` then immediately `nsys export -f csv -t timeline foo.qdrep` to keep artifacts small.
perfbot: note: saved capture IDs: cvp-310123-a and cvp-310123-b attached to the incident ticket.
Aisha: perfect. i'll attach the two qdreps to the ticket and paste the csv diffs after i run them.
Matt: great, ping here when ready and i'll pair on kernel-diff analysis.
